verdict.rationale: Godot is MIT-licensed, and users are the sole copyright owners of their content. Project assets live as ordinary files (images, audio, fonts, scenes) in the local project folder, scripts can be edited in external text editors, and imported derivatives are kept separately in res://.godot/imported/. That makes leaving with your data plausible without vendor lock-in. However, the evidence never documents that Godot's own scene and resource formats are open or text-based, and there is no explicit export-everything or migration path. Missing for 10: documentation that scene/resource files use open or text formats, an explicit data-export or migration workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration of moving a project out of Godot.
